en.title: Netflix Unveils 13 Video Game Adaptations, From PUBG to Diablo
en.summary: The streaming giant is doubling down on its gaming strategy, with a slate of ambitious new projects announced. From Donald Glover's take on PUBG to the long-awaited Diablo series, Netflix is betting big on interactive entertainment.
en.body:
Netflix's video game ambitions have officially exploded. What began with critically acclaimed animated series like **Arcane** and **Castlevania** has now blossomed into a full-scale offensive, encompassing live-action blockbusters and major new partnerships. The platform has confirmed a staggering 13 video game adaptations are currently in various stages of development, signaling a clear intent to dominate the interactive entertainment space on screen.

This expansive strategy includes high-profile projects like **Donald Glover**’s adaptation of **PUBG**, a move that has generated significant buzz among fans of the battle royale giant. Beyond that, the streamer is diving deep into beloved franchises, with **Assassin's Creed** and **Gears of War** set to receive live-action treatments. Recent major partnerships with gaming titans like **SEGA** and **Blizzard** further underscore Netflix's commitment, opening the door for adaptations of iconic worlds like **Diablo**. While specific details on many of these projects remain under wraps, the sheer volume and caliber of the source material indicate a serious investment in captivating the global gaming community.

## From Pixels to Premières

The journey to this current slate has been a long time coming. Netflix has already proven its mettle with a string of successful video game adaptations. Series like **Cyberpunk: Edgerunners**, **Devil May Cry**, **DOTA: Dragon's Blood**, **Dragon Age: Absolution**, and **Tekken: Bloodline** have demonstrated the platform's ability to translate complex game narratives and aesthetics into compelling television. Even lighter fare like **Exploding Kittens** and **Rabbids Invasion: Mission to Mars** have found their audience, showcasing a broad appeal. More mature and visually stunning adaptations such as **Onimusha** and **Castlevania: Nocturne** have cemented Netflix's reputation for quality in this genre. This track record provides a strong foundation for the ambitious slate that lies ahead, reassuring fans that their favorite games are in capable hands.

## Fan Frenzy and Future Stakes

For dedicated fans, this influx of adaptations represents a dream come true, but also a high-stakes gamble. The success of **Arcane**, which transcended its **League of Legends** origins to become a cultural phenomenon, has set an incredibly high bar. The pressure is immense to deliver faithful yet fresh interpretations of beloved universes, balancing fan expectations with the needs of a broader television audience. The cancellation of projects like **The Division** and the uncertainty surrounding **Beyond Good & Evil** serve as stark reminders of the challenges involved. However, the sheer breadth of titles now in development, from massive multiplayer games to beloved RPGs, suggests Netflix is committed to finding its winning formula, ensuring that the passion and lore of these games resonate deeply with viewers worldwide.

## What's Next

With 13 confirmed projects, the immediate future for video game adaptations on Netflix is incredibly bright. While specific release dates are still emerging, the ongoing production and partnership announcements suggest a steady stream of content. Fans should keep a close eye on updates regarding **Diablo**, **Assassin's Creed**, and **PUBG**, as these are poised to be major tentpole releases. The platform's continued investment signals that this is just the beginning of Netflix's journey into the vast landscape of interactive storytelling.

content_raw: Picture Credits: Ubisoft, Microsoft, KRAFTON Netflix’s video game ambitions have never been bigger. What started as a handful of animated adaptations like Castlevania and Arcane has grown into a full-blown strategy, with live-action blockbusters like Assassin’s Creed and Gears of War now in the mix, major new partnerships with SEGA and Blizzard signed in the last few months, and Donald Glover stepping up to adapt PUBG . Below, you’ll find every confirmed video game adaptation we know to be in the works at Netflix, 13 in total, along with where each one stands.  Before we look into what’s coming next, let’s remind ourselves of what video games Netflix has already adapted in the past: Arcane Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix Castlevania & Castlevania: Nocturne Cyberpunk Edgerunners Devil May Cry DOTA: Dragon’s Blood Dragon’s Dogma Dragon Age Exploding Kittens Fate 4pocolypse Monster Hunter: Legends of the Guild Ninokuni Onimusha Rabbids Invasion: Mission to Mars Resident Evil Splinter Cell: Deathwatch Sonic Prime Tekken: Bloodline Tomb Raider: The Legend of Lara Croft Trivia Quest Upcoming Video Game Adaptations A few notes on this one, previously we’d included a few other adaptations, but they’ve been canceled or are thought to be inactive. The Division , we did get confirmation that all plans had been scrapped, for example. Beyond Good and Evil is thought to no longer be moving forward, and while Far Cry was once in development at Netflix (first announced in June 2021), that property is now being adapted at FX/Disney instead . Sticking with Ubisoft, Skull and Bones was another one thought to be in the works at Netflix, but that’s been inactive for a while. Another one that’s gone quiet since its initial 2018 announcement is a live-action movie adaptation of Carmen Sandiego . Mega Man is in the same boat. Steve Blackman was on board to adapt  Horizon: Zero Dawn into a series, although that’s been scrapped and is now in the works as a movie at Sony Pictures.  We won’t be including the League of Legends adaptation Arcane on this list in any great detail, despite a spin-off of some kind  known to be in the works, which we were told by a source  will cover  Iron & Chains .  We’re also not covering returning seasons of existing adaptations in detail, but for the record: Splinter Cell: Deathwatch has a second season on the way, and Devil May Cry will wrap up with a third and final season .
